name: Llama 3.1 8B Instruct
contextNote: Native 128k RoPE; quality solid to ~32k, degrades on long-context recall past ~64k.
kvCacheNote: ~1 GB per 8k ctx (fp16 KV, GQA 8 kv heads); ~0.5 GB with Q8 KV.
goodFor: General-purpose chat/RAG workhorse on any 8GB+ card.
notes: The default 'small local model' baseline. Multilingual (8 languages officially).

name: Llama 3.1 70B Instruct
contextNote: Native 128k; strong to ~32k, usable long-context but recall softens past ~64k.
goodFor: Best general reasoning you can self-host on a single 48GB card at Q4.
notes: Superseded for most uses by Llama 3.3 70B (same size, better quality).

name: Llama 3.2 3B Instruct
contextNote: Native 128k; usable to ~16-32k in practice.
goodFor: Fast local chat / summarization on a 4GB card or a laptop.
notes: Competitive with older 7B models on many tasks.

name: Llama 3.2 11B Vision Instruct
contextNote: 128k text; single-image focused, cross-attention vision adapter on the 8B text core.
kvCacheNote: ~1 GB per 8k ctx + image cross-attn state.
imageNote: Solid captioning, chart/diagram QA, basic doc understanding. MMMU ~50, DocVQA ~88. Weaker OCR than Qwen2.5-VL.
goodFor: General image Q&A on a 12GB card when you want the Llama ecosystem.
notes: llama.cpp/GGUF support lagged and is still imperfect; vLLM/Transformers is the reliable path.

name: Llama 3.3 70B Instruct
contextNote: Native 128k; the best long-context behaviour of the Llama 3 line.
goodFor: Near-405B quality at 70B size; the go-to single-rig open general model of early 2025.
notes: Roughly matches Llama 3.1 405B on many benchmarks. Fits 2x3090/4090 at Q4.

name: Llama 4 Scout 17B-16E
contextNote: Advertised 10M; real long-context quality drops well before that. Practical high-quality window is far smaller (~256k-1M with heavy KV cost).
kvCacheNote: iRoPE + chunked attention keeps KV manageable but 10M ctx is still huge; budget tens of GB for very long ctx.
imageNote: Native early-fusion multimodal. MMMU ~70, strong chart/doc VQA. Multi-image (up to 8 tested).
goodFor: Fast multimodal MoE for a 2x48GB rig; inference speed of a 17B with knowledge of a 100B.
notes: Mixed launch reception; instruction-following and coding weaker than the size suggests.

name: Llama 4 Maverick 17B-128E
contextNote: 1M advertised; usable long-context shorter.
kvCacheNote: 17B active keeps compute cheap; weights dominate VRAM.
minPracticalGPU: 4x80GB (Q4) or heavy CPU offload; not homelab-friendly.
imageNote: MMMU ~73, strong DocVQA/ChartQA. Native multimodal early fusion.
goodFor: Frontier-local multimodal for well-equipped labs; fast per-token thanks to MoE.
notes: LMArena controversy over an experimental chat-tuned variant used for the leaderboard.

name: Qwen2.5 0.5B Instruct
contextNote: 32k native.
goodFor: Draft model for speculative decoding, tiny classifiers, embedded use.
notes: Surprisingly coherent for the size; good spec-decode draft for Qwen2.5 14B/32B/72B.

name: Qwen2.5 7B Instruct
contextNote: 32k native, YaRN to 128k; enable rope scaling for >32k.
goodFor: Strong all-round 8GB model; often beats Llama 3.1 8B on math/code.
notes: One of the most-used local models of 2024-25.

name: Qwen2.5 32B Instruct
contextNote: 32k native, YaRN to 128k.
goodFor: Best single-24GB-card general model of its generation; fits a 3090/4090 at Q4.
notes: Base of DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B and QwQ-32B.

name: Qwen2.5 72B Instruct
contextNote: 32k native, YaRN to 128k.
goodFor: Competes with Llama 3.3 70B; pick on task/benchmark preference.
notes: 72B and 3B carry the Qwen license, not Apache 2.0.

name: Qwen2.5-Coder 7B Instruct
contextNote: 32k native, YaRN to 128k; repo-level fill-in-the-middle trained.
goodFor: Local code completion / FIM in an editor on an 8GB card.
notes: Supports fill-in-the-middle; pair with continue.dev / llama.vim.

name: Qwen2.5-Coder 32B Instruct
contextNote: 32k native, YaRN to 128k.
goodFor: The strongest coding model that fits a single 24GB card; near GPT-4o on HumanEval/code.
notes: Widely used as a local Copilot/Cursor backend in 2025.

name: Qwen2.5-VL 7B Instruct
contextNote: 32k native, extendable; long video / multi-page docs supported.
imageNote: Class-leading open OCR/doc parsing at this size. DocVQA ~95, MMMU ~58, ChartQA ~87. Object grounding, video, agentic GUI.
goodFor: Default local document/screenshot understanding model on an 8-12GB card.
notes: Vision encoder adds ~1-2GB over the base 7B LLM.

name: Qwen2.5-VL 72B Instruct
contextNote: 32k native, extendable.
imageNote: Among the best open VLMs: MMMU ~70, DocVQA ~96, strong agentic GUI / video. Rivals GPT-4o on many vision tasks.
goodFor: Top-tier self-hosted multimodal for a 2x24GB or 48GB rig.
notes: Qwen license (not Apache) for the 72B.

name: Qwen3 8B
contextNote: 32k native, YaRN to 128k. Hybrid reasoning (thinking / non-thinking).
kvCacheNote: ~0.75 GB per 8k ctx; thinking mode consumes many output tokens.
goodFor: Upgraded 8GB workhorse with switchable chain-of-thought.
notes: Thinking mode noticeably boosts math/code at the cost of latency and context budget.

name: Qwen3 32B
contextNote: 32k native, YaRN to 128k. Hybrid reasoning.
goodFor: Best dense model for a single 24GB card in 2025; strong reasoning with thinking on.
notes: Roughly matches Qwen2.5 72B with thinking enabled.

name: Qwen3 30B-A3B
contextNote: 32k native, YaRN to 128k. Hybrid reasoning.
kvCacheNote: ~0.5 GB per 8k ctx; only 3B active so it is very fast even CPU/partial-offload.
minPracticalGPU: 24 GB (Q4) or 16GB + CPU offload; runs well on Apple Silicon.
goodFor: Near-32B quality at ~10x the speed; excellent CPU/partial-offload option.
notes: A 2025 community favourite for its speed/quality/VRAM balance. Refreshed as 30B-A3B-2507 (better).

name: Qwen3 235B-A22B
contextNote: 32k native, YaRN to 128k. Hybrid reasoning. Later 2507 variants split Instruct/Thinking and push to 256k.
kvCacheNote: 22B active keeps compute modest; weights dominate. Dynamic 2-3 bit quants land ~90-110GB.
minPracticalGPU: 2x80GB (Q4) or 128GB+ unified memory / heavy CPU offload.
goodFor: Frontier-local reasoning for a big rig or a 128GB Mac Studio / Strix Halo box.
notes: Competes with DeepSeek-R1 / early GPT-4-class on reasoning. 2507 refresh is markedly better.

name: Qwen3-VL 8B Instruct
contextNote: 256k native, expandable toward 1M; strong long-video / multi-doc retention.
kvCacheNote: ~0.75 GB per 8k text ctx + visual tokens; long video is KV-heavy.
imageNote: Improves on Qwen2.5-VL: better OCR (32 languages), spatial grounding, GUI agent, video. Instruct and Thinking variants.
goodFor: Current best small local VLM for docs/screenshots/GUI agents on a 12GB card.
notes: Family spans 2B/4B/8B/32B dense + 30B-A3B / 235B-A22B MoE. Released Sept-Oct 2025.

name: Qwen2-Audio 7B Instruct
contextNote: 32k text; audio input up to ~30s segments (Whisper-style encoder).
kvCacheNote: ~0.75 GB per 8k ctx + audio encoder state.
audioNote: Voice chat + audio analysis (speech, sound events, music). ASR is decent but not SOTA WER; strength is audio Q&A/reasoning, not pure transcription. ~8 spoken languages.
goodFor: Local 'ask questions about this audio clip' on a 12GB card.
notes: Superseded by Qwen2.5-Omni for full omni use.

name: Mistral Nemo 12B Instruct 2407
contextNote: 128k native; strong to ~32k, softens further out.
goodFor: Multilingual 12GB chat model; Tekken tokenizer is efficient on non-English.
notes: Popular fine-tune base (e.g. for roleplay). FP8-friendly by design.

name: Mistral Small 3.2 24B Instruct 2506
contextNote: 128k native.
imageNote: Vision added in 3.1; 3.2 improves instruction-following and reduces repetition. MMMU ~observed mid-60s. Good general VQA, decent OCR.
goodFor: Apache-licensed 24B multimodal that fits one 24GB card; strong function calling.
notes: Mistral Small 3 (Jan 2025) was text-only; 3.1 (Mar) added vision + 128k; 3.2 (Jun) is a quality patch.

name: Mixtral 8x22B Instruct v0.1
contextNote: 64k native.
goodFor: Large Apache MoE; superseded by DeepSeek V3 / Qwen3 235B on quality-per-VRAM.
notes: Native function calling. Big VRAM footprint for the quality it delivers today.

name: Pixtral 12B (2409)
contextNote: 128k text; native-resolution ViT (400M) handles arbitrary aspect ratios, multi-image.
imageNote: MMMU ~52, good ChartQA/DocVQA (~90). Strong instruction-following on images; OCR below Qwen2.5-VL.
goodFor: Apache multimodal on a 12-16GB card with the Mistral tokenizer/ecosystem.
notes: Built on Nemo 12B. vLLM has the best support.

name: Ministral 8B Instruct 2410
contextNote: 128k native; interleaved sliding-window attention for efficiency.
goodFor: Edge / on-device chat; note the non-commercial license on the open weights.
notes: Ministral 3B weights were not openly released; 8B weights are research-license only.

name: Voxtral Mini 3B 2507
contextNote: 32k text; up to ~30 min audio for transcription, ~40 min for understanding.
kvCacheNote: audio tokenized at ~12.5 Hz keeps long audio affordable.
audioNote: Built on Ministral 3B. Beats Whisper-large-v3 on several benchmarks (English short-form, Common Voice); also does audio Q&A, summarization, translation. 8+ languages with auto language detection.
goodFor: Local transcription + 'ask about this recording' on a 6-8GB card.
notes: Also supports voice-triggered function calling.

name: Voxtral Small 24B 2507
contextNote: 32k text; ~30-40 min audio input.
audioNote: Built on Mistral Small 3.1 24B; retains strong text ability. State-of-the-art open audio understanding, beats GPT-4o mini Transcribe / Gemini 2.5 Flash on transcription. Multilingual.
goodFor: Production-grade local speech understanding on a 24GB card that also handles text tasks.
notes: Text vision from Small 3.1 is NOT retained in Voxtral (audio-only multimodal).

name: Devstral Small 1.1 (24B)
contextNote: 128k native; tuned for agentic coding / repo navigation.
goodFor: Best open agentic-coding model for a single 24GB card; tops SWE-bench Verified among small open models (~53%).
notes: Built on Mistral Small 3.1. Designed to drive OpenHands / SWE-agent loops locally.

name: Gemma 2 9B Instruction-Tuned
contextNote: 8k native only.
goodFor: Strong chat / writing quality on an 8GB card, if 8k context is enough.
notes: Was a LMArena favourite for its size in 2024. SWA + logit soft-capping.

name: Gemma 3 4B Instruction-Tuned
contextNote: 128k native (32k for 1B). SigLIP vision encoder, images at 896x896 / pan-and-scan.
kvCacheNote: ~0.4 GB per 8k ctx thanks to 5:1 local/global attention.
minPracticalGPU: 6 GB (Q4) - QAT int4 needs even less
imageNote: Good captions / VQA / basic OCR for the size. MMMU ~48. Weaker at dense document OCR than Qwen2.5-VL.
goodFor: Small multimodal chat on a 6GB card; 140+ languages; official QAT quant.
notes: Function calling supported. Great multilingual coverage.

name: Gemma 3 12B Instruction-Tuned
contextNote: 128k native.
imageNote: MMMU ~59, decent DocVQA. Good general VQA and chart reading; OCR trails Qwen2.5-VL 7B.
goodFor: Well-rounded 12GB multimodal chat with strong multilingual + long context.
notes: Ships an official QAT int4 checkpoint (~7GB).

name: Gemma 3 27B Instruction-Tuned
contextNote: 128k native.
imageNote: MMMU ~65, strong general VQA / chart / diagram reasoning. Good but not best-in-class OCR.
goodFor: Top single-24GB multimodal chat model; LMArena ~1340, near much larger models.
notes: Official QAT int4 (~14-15GB) is the recommended way to run it on a 24GB card with context.

name: Gemma 3n E4B Instruction-Tuned
contextNote: 32k. Per-Layer Embeddings offload lets an 8B-param model run in a ~4B memory budget.
kvCacheNote: designed for phones; footprint closer to a 4B model.
imageNote: MobileNet-V5 vision encoder; good on-device captions / VQA / OCR for size.
audioNote: USM-based audio encoder: on-device ASR and speech translation, ~6 languages well-supported; short-form focused.
goodFor: On-device omni assistant (text+image+voice) for phones / 4-6GB machines.
notes: E2B variant is smaller (~2B effective). MatFormer allows mix-and-match sizing.

name: DeepSeek-V3-0324
contextNote: 128k native; MLA + DeepSeekMoE. Original V3 was Dec 2024; 0324 is a strong refresh.
kvCacheNote: MLA keeps KV tiny; unsloth dynamic 1.6-2.7 bit quants run in ~140-250GB (fits a 192-256GB Mac Studio / EPYC box).
minPracticalGPU: 8x80GB (Q4) or 192GB+ unified memory with dynamic quant; ~37B active
goodFor: Frontier-class open weights; runs (slowly) on a high-RAM CPU box or big Mac via dynamic quant.
notes: FP8-native training. The reference point for 'best open non-reasoning model' in 2025.

name: DeepSeek-R1-0528
contextNote: 128k native; long reasoning traces consume large output-token budgets.
kvCacheNote: MLA keeps KV small; unsloth 1.5-2 bit dynamic quants ~150-220GB.
goodFor: Best open reasoning model of 2025; near o1/o3-mini on math and code.
notes: R1-0528 is a large quality bump over the Jan 2025 R1. MIT licensed, distillation explicitly allowed.

name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B
contextNote: Inherits Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B (32k native; long reasoning eats output tokens).
goodFor: Tiny model that punches way above weight on math (AIME ~28%, MATH ~83%).
notes: Narrow: strong at math/logic, weak at general chat/knowledge. Verbose reasoning.

name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-32B
contextNote: Qwen2.5-32B base; 32k native, YaRN to 128k.
kvCacheNote: ~1 GB per 8k ctx + large output budget for reasoning traces.
goodFor: Best reasoning model that fits one 24GB card; beats o1-mini on AIME/MATH.
notes: A 2025 homelab staple. QwQ-32B is a similar-niche alternative.

name: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B
contextNote: Llama 3.3 70B base; 128k native.
kvCacheNote: ~1.25 GB per 8k ctx + long reasoning output.
goodFor: Top open reasoning quality for a 2x24GB rig without the 671B footprint.
notes: Roughly o1-mini-class on math/code; carries the Llama license from its base.

name: Phi-3.5-mini Instruct
contextNote: 128k native (LongRoPE); strong for a small model but recall drops past ~32k.
goodFor: MIT-licensed 128k small model for a 4GB card; strong reasoning-per-param, thin world knowledge.
notes: Synthetic-heavy training: good at reasoning/format, weaker on trivia and can be over-cautious.

name: Phi-4 (14B)
contextNote: Only 16k native - short vs peers. A later Phi-4 'mini' / reasoning line differs.
goodFor: MIT 14B with strong STEM/math reasoning for its size on a 12GB card.
notes: 16k context and modest tool use are the tradeoffs. Excellent GPQA/MATH for 14B.

name: Phi-4-multimodal Instruct
contextNote: 128k text; LoRA adapters for vision and speech on a 3.8B language core.
imageNote: Good OCR / chart / document reasoning for 5.6B; competitive with much larger VLMs on some doc tasks.
audioNote: Strong ASR: topped OpenASR leaderboard at release (~6.1% avg WER), plus speech translation and audio Q&A. ~8 languages for ASR.
goodFor: Single small MIT model that does text + image + best-in-class small-model ASR on a 6-8GB card.
notes: Speech and vision adapters can be loaded independently.

name: Command R (35B) 08-2024
contextNote: 128k native; built for RAG with citation output and grounded generation.
kvCacheNote: ~2 GB per 8k ctx - no GQA in the original, KV is heavy; the 08-2024 refresh improved this.
goodFor: RAG / tool-use with built-in inline citations on a 24GB card; non-commercial license.
notes: Strong multilingual (10 languages) and structured tool-calling; KV cache larger than peers.

name: Command R+ (104B) 08-2024
contextNote: 128k native; multi-step tool use and RAG citations.
goodFor: Agentic multi-step tool use + grounded RAG for a multi-GPU rig; non-commercial.
notes: One of the earliest models purpose-built for agent workflows.

name: Command R7B (12-2024)
contextNote: 128k native; sliding-window + global attention.
goodFor: Smallest Command model; RAG + tool use + 23 languages on an 8GB card, non-commercial.
notes: Good multilingual retrieval assistant; general reasoning behind Qwen2.5 7B.

name: Aya Expanse 32B
contextNote: 128k native (based on Command R architecture).
goodFor: Best-in-class open multilingual coverage (23 languages) on a 24GB card.
notes: Aya Vision 8B/32B (2025) adds multimodal. Non-commercial license.

name: InternVL3 14B
contextNote: 32k typical; native multimodal pre-training (V2PE position encoding).
kvCacheNote: ~1 GB per 8k ctx + visual tokens (dynamic tiling can add many).
imageNote: MMMU ~65-70, DocVQA ~94, strong OCR / multi-image / video / grounding. One of the top open VLM families.
goodFor: Top-tier open image understanding on a 16GB card; sizes 1B-78B available.
notes: InternVL2.5 and InternVL2 are the prior generations; 3 is the one to use.

name: MiniCPM-V 2.6 (8B)
license: MiniCPM Model License (free commercial with registration)
contextNote: 32k; Qwen2 7B + SigLIP. Multi-image and video (up to ~64 frames).
kvCacheNote: ~0.75 GB per 8k ctx + visual tokens; efficient token compression (~64 tok/frame).
imageNote: Punches above weight: OCRBench SOTA-for-size at release, DocVQA ~90, MMMU ~49. Efficient visual tokenization = many frames cheaply.
goodFor: Efficient OCR / multi-image / video understanding on an 8GB card; strong llama.cpp support.
notes: Popular for local OCR pipelines before Qwen2.5-VL.

name: MiniCPM-o 2.6 (8B)
license: MiniCPM Model License (free commercial with registration)
contextNote: 32k; streaming video + audio in, text + speech out. Real-time bilingual (EN/ZH) voice.
kvCacheNote: ~0.75 GB per 8k ctx + vision/audio encoders + TTS head.
imageNote: Vision comparable to MiniCPM-V 2.6 / GPT-4o-mini level: OCRBench high, DocVQA ~90, MMMU ~50.
audioNote: Bilingual real-time speech conversation, voice cloning, emotion control; ASR competitive with Whisper-large-v3 on EN/ZH. End-to-end speech out.
goodFor: Local GPT-4o-style live voice+vision assistant on a 12-16GB card.
notes: Full omni (speech out) needs the reference stack; llama.cpp only covers the vision path.

name: GLM-4.1V-9B-Thinking
contextNote: 64k; GLM-4-9B base + vision, reasoning ('thinking') tuned with RL.
imageNote: MMMU ~68, strong on chart/STEM/diagram reasoning and GUI agents; outperforms much larger VLMs on reasoning-heavy vision tasks. Video + grounding.
goodFor: Best small open VLM for visual reasoning / GUI agents on a 12GB card.
notes: GLM-4V-9B (2024) is the non-thinking predecessor.

name: Molmo 7B-D
contextNote: Short ~4k text context - a real limitation for multi-turn / doc work.
imageNote: Qwen2 7B + OpenAI CLIP. Strong natural-image VQA and unique 'pointing' (2D coordinate) ability. OCR/doc weaker; trained on the open PixMo dataset.
goodFor: Fully-open-data VLM with pointing/grounding for robotics / UI on a 12GB card.
notes: Value is openness + pointing, not raw benchmark lead. MolmoE-1B and Molmo-72B also exist.

name: Llama-3.1-Nemotron-70B-Instruct
contextNote: 128k native (from Llama 3.1 70B base).
goodFor: RLHF-heavy Llama 70B tune that topped Arena Hard / AlpacaEval in late 2024; great chat feel.
notes: Reward-model-guided alignment (HelpSteer2). Not better at raw knowledge than Llama 3.3 70B.

name: Granite 3.1 8B Instruct
contextNote: 128k native (3.1 extended it from 4k in 3.0).
goodFor: Enterprise-friendly Apache model with clean data provenance; solid tool-calling / RAG on 8GB.
notes: Also a 3B-A800M / 1B-A400M MoE and Granite 3.2 with reasoning. Granite Vision 3.2 2B for docs.

name: OLMo 2 13B Instruct
contextNote: 4k native - the main practical limitation.
goodFor: Fully-open model (data, code, checkpoints) for research/reproducibility, not for long-context work.
notes: Matches Llama 3.1 8B / Qwen2.5 7B tier at release. OLMo 2 32B (2025) is bigger and better.

name: SmolLM2 1.7B Instruct
contextNote: 8k native.
goodFor: Fully-open small model for edge / browser / in-app use; strong for 1.7B.
notes: SmolVLM (2B / 256M / 500M) is the multimodal sibling and is a great tiny-VLM option.

name: Falcon-Mamba 7B Instruct
contextNote: Pure SSM (Mamba-2): no attention, constant memory regardless of sequence length - context is bounded by compute/quality not KV cache. Trained mostly at 8k.
kvCacheNote: No KV cache - fixed-size recurrent state. This is the headline feature: flat memory as context grows.
goodFor: Demonstration of attention-free long-context on modest VRAM; quality trails Transformer 7Bs.
notes: In-context retrieval over very long inputs is weaker than attention models despite the memory advantage.

name: Jamba 1.5 Mini
contextNote: 256k native, effective long-context helped by the Mamba layers; KV cache far smaller than a pure Transformer at long ctx.
kvCacheNote: Hybrid SSM/attention: ~1/8th the KV of a comparable Transformer at 256k - the main selling point.
minPracticalGPU: 32-48 GB (Q4) for full model; long ctx adds relatively little
goodFor: Very long-document RAG / summarization where KV cache would otherwise blow up VRAM.
notes: Jamba 1.5 Large (398B-A94B) is the bigger sibling. Weaker on short-task benchmarks than same-size dense.

name: Whisper large-v3
contextNote: Processes fixed 30-second windows; long audio handled by chunking + timestamp stitching.
kvCacheNote: Tiny decoder KV; VRAM is dominated by the encoder. faster-whisper (CTranslate2) int8 runs in ~1-1.5GB.
minPracticalGPU: 2 GB (int8) / runs on CPU at ~1x realtime
audioNote: ~99 languages. English WER ~2-5% clean, worse in noise/accent. Multilingual varies widely. RTF ~0.1-0.3 on a modern GPU (faster-whisper). Hallucinates on silence/music. No speaker diarization.
goodFor: The default local transcription workhorse; use whisper.cpp or faster-whisper, not the reference repo.
notes: large-v3 added a language token and 128 mel bins vs v2; slightly more hallucination-prone than v2 for some.

name: Whisper large-v3-turbo
contextNote: 30-second windows; decoder cut from 32 to 4 layers.
audioNote: ~8x faster than large-v3 for a small WER increase (roughly +0.5-1% absolute on many sets). Multilingual, though a touch weaker than v3 on some low-resource languages. RTF often <0.05 on GPU.
goodFor: Near-real-time local transcription; the practical default over large-v3 for most homelab use.
notes: Not trained on the translation task (transcription only).

name: Distil-Whisper large-v3.5
contextNote: 30-second windows; 2-layer decoder distilled from large-v3.
audioNote: English-only. Within ~1% WER of large-v3 on English, ~6x faster, less prone to hallucination/repetition. RTF very low. Good speculative-decoding draft for large-v3.
goodFor: Fast English-only local transcription, or as an assistant model to speed up full Whisper.
notes: Earlier distil-large-v2 / v3 and distil-medium.en / small.en also exist.

name: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v2
contextNote: FastConformer encoder + TDT (token-and-duration Transducer) decoder; handles up to ~24 min in one pass.
kvCacheNote: Transducer, not autoregressive LM - no KV cache; VRAM is encoder activations. ~2GB typical.
audioNote: English only (v2). #1 on HF Open ASR Leaderboard at release, ~6.05% avg WER. Extremely fast: RTFx ~3380 (transcribes ~60 min of audio in ~1 s on an A100). Word/char timestamps, auto punctuation/capitalization. v3 (Sept 2025) adds 25 languages.
goodFor: Blazing-fast, accurate English batch transcription on a small NVIDIA GPU (or Apple Silicon via parakeet-mlx).
notes: NeMo dependency is heavier to set up than whisper.cpp. English-only in v2.

name: NVIDIA Canary 1B v2
contextNote: FastConformer encoder + Transformer decoder (attention encoder-decoder); segment-based for long audio.
audioNote: 25 European languages + speech translation (X<->En). Beats Whisper-large-v3 on avg WER (~7.15%) at ~7-10x the speed (RTFx ~749). Timestamps supported. Broader language set trades a little English accuracy vs Parakeet.
goodFor: Fast local multilingual ASR + speech translation on a small NVIDIA GPU.
notes: Canary-1B-flash and Canary-180M-flash are faster/smaller variants; earlier Canary-1B covered 4 languages.

name: Moonshine Base
contextNote: Encoder-decoder; no fixed 30s window - compute scales with actual audio length (unlike Whisper's padded 30s).
kvCacheNote: Negligible; designed for microcontrollers / edge CPUs.
minPracticalGPU: none needed - runs on Raspberry Pi / phone CPU
audioNote: English only (tiny 27M / base 61M). WER comparable to Whisper tiny/base; ~5x faster on short utterances because it doesn't pad to 30s. Built for streaming/wake-word/edge voice UIs.
goodFor: Always-on low-latency English voice commands on edge hardware with no GPU.
notes: Not for high-accuracy long-form transcription - use Whisper/Parakeet for that.

name: Ultravox v0.5 (Llama 3.1 8B)
contextNote: 128k text (from Llama 3.1 8B); audio projected directly into the LLM via a Whisper-encoder adapter - no ASR step.
audioNote: Speech-in / text-out; understands and reasons about spoken input with ~150ms time-to-first-token. Not optimized for verbatim transcription WER - it's a speech-native LLM for voice agents. No speech output (pair with a TTS).
goodFor: Low-latency local voice-agent brain (speech in, text out) on a 12GB card.
notes: Also built on Llama 3.3 70B and Qwen2.5 variants. Adapter is MIT; base model license applies.

name: Kyutai STT 2.6B (English)
contextNote: Streaming delayed-streams architecture; designed for real-time incremental transcription with a fixed short delay.
kvCacheNote: Streaming model; modest fixed state. ~2GB at bf16 in practice per Kyutai.
audioNote: English (2.6B) or English+French (1B). Built for low-latency streaming with semantic VAD; WER competitive with Whisper-large-v3 on English. Word-level timestamps. Powers Kyutai's Unmute/Moshi voice stack.
goodFor: Real-time streaming English transcription for live captioning / voice agents.
notes: The 1B en/fr model needs even less VRAM. Batching allows hundreds of real-time streams on one GPU.

name: Wan 2.2 T2V-A14B
goodFor: Best open photoreal video, esp. humans/faces. 5s 720p clips; T2V + I2V.
notes: Quality leader among open models Sep 2026. MoE-style dual expert (high/low noise). Also 14B I2V, S2V, Animate variants.

name: Wan 2.2 TI2V-5B
goodFor: The one that actually fits a 12 GB card. T2V + I2V, 720p ~5s.
notes: Same family as the 14B, big quality drop but genuinely consumer-runnable.

name: HunyuanVideo 1.5
goodFor: Cinematic motion + prompt adherence; beats Gen-3 in blind tests.
notes: v1.5 cut VRAM hard vs the original 13B. Non-commercial-ish community license (regional restrictions).

name: LTX-2.3
goodFor: Only open model with NATIVE synced audio + video in one diffusion pass. 4K @ 50 fps.
notes: The audio comes out of the same model — no separate step. Heavy: distilled build needs a 5090/A6000.

name: LTX-Video 0.9.8 (2B)
goodFor: Fastest open video — near real-time on a 4090. Lower fidelity than Wan/Hunyuan.
notes: The small predecessor to LTX-2. Great for iteration / previz on modest hardware. No native audio.

name: CogVideoX-5B
goodFor: 6s 720p; the low-VRAM baseline before Wan 2.2 5B. I2V variant available.
notes: Aging but very lightweight and well-supported in diffusers. 2B variant is Apache-2.0.

name: Mochi 1
goodFor: Strong motion realism, permissive Apache license. T2V only.
notes: One of the first genuinely good Apache-2.0 video models. Heavy; largely superseded by Wan 2.2.

name: Open-Sora 2.0
goodFor: Fully open (weights + training code + data recipe). Research / fine-tuning base.
notes: Trained for ~$200k and open about it. Quality below Wan/Hunyuan but the most reproducible.

name: ACE-Step
goodFor: Full songs with vocals + instrumental, up to ~4 min. Fast on consumer GPUs.
notes: Diffusion music foundation model. Lyric + style prompt -> song. The go-to open Suno alternative that fits 12 GB.

name: YuE 7B
goodFor: Closest open thing to Suno for full vocal tracks; better vocals than ACE-Step, much slower.
notes: Autoregressive (LLaMA-based) two-stage. Minutes of generation time per song on a 4090.

name: MusicGen Large
goodFor: Instrumental loops / beds up to ~30 s; melody-conditioning variant.
notes: Old but rock-solid and tiny. No vocals. Non-commercial license on the weights.

name: Stable Audio Open 1.0
goodFor: Sound effects, foley, drum loops, short samples (up to 47 s).
notes: Trained only on licensed audio (Freesound / FMA). Not for full songs — samples and SFX.

name: Kokoro-82M
goodFor: Best quality-per-size TTS. Runs real-time on CPU. Preset voices, several languages.
notes: No voice cloning (fixed voice bank). The default for local narration / AudioComic-style pipelines.

name: Orpheus TTS 3B
goodFor: Zero-shot voice cloning + guided emotion tags (<laugh>, <sigh>). Low latency, streamable.
notes: A Llama-3.2-3B backbone speech LLM — runs on the same stacks as a normal LLM.

name: Chatterbox
goodFor: Voice clone from ~5 s of audio + an "emotion exaggeration" dial. MIT licensed.
notes: Resemble claims 63% preference vs ElevenLabs in their own test. English only.

name: Dia 1.6B
goodFor: Multi-speaker dialogue in one pass, with laughs/coughs/nonverbals. [S1]/[S2] tags.
notes: Purpose-built for podcast / conversation synthesis rather than single-voice narration.

name: CSM-1B
goodFor: Conversational speech with context (prior turns condition prosody). ~4.7 MOS.
notes: Backbone of Sesame’s voice demo. Needs conversation context to sound its best; bare single-shot is plainer.

name: F5-TTS
goodFor: Fast flow-matching voice clone from a short reference. English + Chinese.
notes: Very light, widely integrated. Good default when Chatterbox’s license or Orpheus’s size are a problem.
